issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify addGuestStudents(int, String) (an int plus a reason String), but the solution implements addGuestStudents(int) with only a single int parameter. This parameter mismatch means students following the specification (or the tests) expecting a two-parameter method will be unable to use the provided solution signature and will be confused about the correct method contract.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the implementation with the specification: change the solution's addGuestStudents method to have the signature addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, String reason) and handle or record the reason (even if only by ignoring it or logging it). Alternatively, if the intention is to only accept an int, update the problem statement and UML to specify addGuestStudents(int) to avoid mismatch.

issues.description: The problem statement specifies a method addGuestStudents(int, String) (an int for new guests and a String reason), but the solution implements addGuestStudents(int) with only a single int parameter. The template contains a TODO for addGuestStudents but no concrete signature. This mismatch in the method signature (presence/absence of the 'reason' parameter and its identifier) creates a mapping barrier: students reading the requirements will expect to implement or use a two-parameter method, while the provided solution uses a one-parameter method.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the method signature across artifacts. Either update the solution (and template) to implement addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, String reason) — keeping the parameter names as in the problem statement — or change the problem statement to require addGuestStudents(int) if the reason parameter is intentionally omitted. Preferred fix: implement public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, String reason) in Lecture and use/store/log the reason so the signature matches the exercise description.
